subject: Clarify: Billing anchor for hybrid token usage and discount tiers
messages:
From: Amy Chen <amy@brightcart.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Billing questions for hybrid usage patterns

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Brightcart’s engineering and procurement teams reviewed the workload profile and we have a few concrete billing questions before we finalize the pilot commit. The short version: our usage mixes very short per-user calls (~30 tokens) and long context summarization jobs (~12k tokens) and we want to understand how that maps to your billing units and how discounts will apply.

Could you confirm the following so we can sign off on the PO?

1) Rounding granularity: do you round up per API call, per session/conversation, or per billing window? For streaming responses, is rounding applied on the final token count or on interim chunks?

2) Context length accounting: for a single request with 12k tokens (input+output), is that billed as one 12k unit, or split into multiple units (16k, 8k) depending on model and packaging? If split, how do minimums and floors apply across the splits?

3) Discounts & anchor: our procurement needs an anchor to calculate blended price tiers. If we commit to 1.5B tokens/month, what discount bands apply and are the discounts applied before or after rounding (i.e., does rounding inflate the committed usage)?

4) KV/prefix reuse credits: can you explain how warm KV cache reuse reduces billable tokens (if at all) and whether you apply credits to the same billing line or as an invoice-level rebate?

We attached a sample usage histogram (internal) in case that helps. If you can share a short sample invoice showing a mixed workload and the math, that'd be ideal.

Appreciate a clear worked example we can hand to our finance team.

Thanks,
Amy
Amy Chen
Senior Procurement Manager
Brightcart

Attachments: brightcart_usage_histogram.csv (stub)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Amy Chen <amy@brightcart.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Billing questions for hybrid usage patterns

Hi Amy — great questions and thanks for the histogram, that helps a lot. Looping in Vanessa and Karthik from pricing and Tessa from solutions so we can give a single worked example.

High level answers up front, followed by a short worked example below:

- Rounding: our canonical billing unit is per-request post-tokenization; rounding is applied at the request level by default (we round up to the nearest billing quantum for each API call). We offer a per-session aggregation option for enterprise commits (roll-up within a conversation window) if customers want to avoid per-call inflation. For streaming, we bill on final realized tokens for the request (we don't round interim chunks).

- Context splitting: a single 12k request will be billed against the model's supported bucket sizes. For example, if using a model packaged as 8k/16k variants, the request will map to the 16k equivalent and be billed as that single 16k unit unless the customer opts into a split-and-bill policy (we can split into smaller units but minimums apply per-split).

- Discounts & anchor: discounts are applied to the net billable tokens after rounding (so rounding can slightly inflate what the discount base sees). For committed anchors we can apply blended tier discounts to committed units with true-ups monthly.

- KV/prefix credits: KV reuse is eligible for prefix-credits which we apply as an invoice-level credit line (not as negative line-items on individual requests).

Worked example (Brightcart sample workload):
- Sample day: 10k short calls at 30 tokens each (API-call rounding quantum = 64 tokens), 400 long summarization jobs at 12k tokens each.

Per-call rounding math: short calls: 30 -> rounded to 64 => per short call billed = 64 tokens. 10k * 64 = 640k tokens/day.
Long jobs: 12k sized request -> maps to 16k bucket (single unit) => 400 * 16k = 6.4M tokens/day.
Total billed tokens/day = 7.04M -> monthly (~30 days) ~211M tokens billed.

If you commit to 1.5B tokens/month and we apply a 10% tier discount, discount is calculated on the 211M monthly billable tokens (after rounding) and then the invoice shows discounts on the invoice-level. True-up reconciles committed vs actual at month end.

Vanessa / Karthik — can you confirm the discount bands for a 1.5B anchor and whether we have flexibility on applying rounding at the session level for Brightcart?

Next steps: Vanessa will draft a short sample invoice + discount matrix and Tessa can produce a customer-facing one-pager that Brightcart can hand to finance. Amy — once you confirm the PO window (monthly/quarterly commit) we can include the session-rollup option in the SOW.

Cheers,
Dylan
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Amy Chen <amy@brightcart.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 13:21:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Billing questions for hybrid usage patterns

Amy, Dylan — putting the worked example into a few concrete lines and attaching an example workbook. I also added two optional concession knobs we typically use for mixed short/long workloads.

Summary of policy points (short):
1) Rounding quantum = 64 tokens by default (per-request). We can change to 1) per-session aggregation (roll-up within a conversation id/window up to 24h) or 2) per-invoice aggregation for committed customers as a contract addendum. Session aggregation removes per-call rounding for short bursts.

2) Large single requests map to the nearest higher bucket for the model packaging (we do not split automatically unless requested). Example: 12k -> 16k. If you want fine-grained split billing we can enable split-and-bill, but each split is still subject to the billing quantum and minimums.

3) Discounts & anchor math: the committed anchor is expressed in billable tokens (post-rounding). Discount bands for a 1.5B anchor (standard sheet):
   - 0 - 250M: list price
   - 250M - 750M: 8% discount
   - 750M - 1.5B: 12% discount
   - >1.5B: 15% discount
Discounts apply to billable tokens after rounding. Monthly true-up reconciles actuals vs commit; overage billed at the negotiated overage rate or deducted from prepaid bucket (if prepay).

4) KV/prefix credits: we offer a prefix-credit policy: when the same prefix is reused within a configured horizon (default 6h), we apply per-prefix credits (line-item on the invoice) equal to the tokens saved by KV reuse. Credits show as separate invoice lines and do not reduce the commit anchor directly — they reduce net billed tokens on invoice.

Optional concession for Brightcart (given mixed short/long):
- Concession A: session-aggregation enabled by default for the pilot (removes per-call rounding for short calls).
- Concession B: 10% one-time onboarding credit applied to first invoice to compensate for early rounding inflation while you ramp up.

Attached: billing_examples_brightcart.xlsx (worked example with day/week/month tabs), discount_matrix_v1.pdf (band definitions), draft_DocuSign_SOW.docx (SOW with session-aggregation clause).

Next steps (small MRAP):
- Amy: confirm preferred commit cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and whether you want session-aggregation enabled for pilot.
- If yes, we’ll issue SOW draft and DocuSign link.

Happy to jump on a 20-min call to walk through the workbook if it helps.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail our finance team needs. Two quick follow-ups:

1) For streaming summarization jobs that produce tokens incrementally, just to confirm you bill on final realized token count (so no interim rounding)? That eliminates a lot of ambiguity for our engineering team.

2) We'd like the session-aggregation concession for the 90-day pilot. Please issue the SOW and DocuSign link and we will circulate internally once the final banding confirms.

If you can include the 10% onboarding credit as a line in the SOW that would make procurement happy.

We can sign electronically once the SOW is updated.

Best,
Amy
Senior Procurement Manager
Brightcart
